title: Space Force awards five companies $60 million for multi-vendor satellite network tests
summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded five companies a total of $60 million to prototype and test connections to a SpaceX-built data network backbone for a multi-vendor satellite network. The companies involved are Amazon Leo, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Rocket Lab, and York Space.

title: Space Command expands Alabama footprint as headquarters relocation advances
summary: Space Command is expanding its presence in Alabama with over 100 personnel relocated to Redstone Arsenal. Construction of a billion-dollar facility is set to begin as the headquarters relocation progresses.

title: An optical link ‘internet’ to connect networks in space
summary: Mbryonics' CEO John Mackey discusses building optical links for satellites and space infrastructure to create an 'internet' in space. The conversation highlights the technology's potential to connect networks beyond Earth.

title: Maritime Satellite Service Revenues to Reach $3.79 Billion by 2035 as NGSO Reshapes Maritime Connectivity
summary: The maritime satellite communications market is projected to reach $3.79 billion by 2035 due to advancements in next-generation satellite networks (NGSO) enhancing maritime connectivity. Novaspace's latest report highlights this significant growth trend.

title: Paragon lays off staff after Gateway cancellation
summary: Paragon Space Development Corporation laid off 70 employees following NASA's cancellation of work on the lunar Gateway program. The company was a subcontractor for a module under development for the Gateway.

title: Astranis unveils geostationary surveillance satellite
summary: Astranis has introduced a new geostationary surveillance satellite designed to inspect, track, and maneuver around other satellites in geostationary orbit. This spacecraft aims to enhance space situational awareness and satellite servicing capabilities.

title: Virgin Galactic delays resumption of commercial flights to 2027
summary: Virgin Galactic has delayed the resumption of its commercial suborbital spaceplane flights to early 2027, pushing back the timeline by a few months.

title: Space Force orders two more Impulse Space vehicles for maneuvering demonstrations
summary: The U.S. Space Force has expanded a contract by $28 million to order two additional Impulse Space vehicles for maneuvering demonstrations. These vehicles, Victus Salo 2 and 3, will support responsive-space missions.

title: Pentagon missile buildup changing the factory floor
summary: Startups are introducing commercial space technologies like software, robotics, and advanced manufacturing to the defense industry to accelerate missile production. This shift is driven by Pentagon pressure to rapidly scale up missile manufacturing.

title: Space Command identifies capabilities it needs for the next space war
summary: Space Command has identified offensive capabilities needed for future space warfare, specifically targeting the critical nodes of large satellite constellations. Gen. Stephen Whiting has urged the industry to develop methods to disable these nodes.

title: NASA astronaut Mike Fincke retires after 30 years at the space agency
summary: NASA astronaut Mike Fincke has retired after 30 years of service, marking the end of a distinguished career that included commanding the International Space Station twice and leading the Astronaut Office’s Commercial Crew Branch.

title: Supermassive black hole spews energy 300,000 light years into deep space
summary: A supermassive black hole has been observed emitting energy spanning 300,000 light years into space, which is three times the length of the Milky Way galaxy. This discovery provides new insights into the powerful phenomena associated with black holes.

title: NASA's canceled lunar space station tech will help build the Artemis moon base
summary: Northrop Grumman will repurpose technology from NASA's canceled lunar space station for the Artemis moon base. The HALO module's technology will be adapted for this new mission.

title: 'The X-Files' creator Chris Carter says new director's cut of 'I Want to Believe' is 'the horror movie that we really wanted to make' (interview)
summary: Chris Carter, creator of 'The X-Files', is releasing a new R-rated director's cut of the 2008 film 'I Want to Believe' on Hulu. The re-edited version aims to reflect the original horror vision he had for the movie.

title: How to image the planets with a telescope and camera
summary: A tutorial provides a step-by-step guide on photographing planets like Jupiter, Saturn, Mars, and Venus using a telescope and camera. It focuses on practical techniques for amateur astronomers and astrophotographers.

title: Virgin Galactic delays next commercial spaceflight to 2027
summary: Virgin Galactic has delayed its next commercial spaceflight to February 2027, marking a further postponement from its previous schedule. The company last conducted a spaceflight in June 2024.

title: The Perseid meteor shower peak was spectacular: Here are our favorite photos
summary: The Perseid meteor shower reached its peak, showcasing spectacular views captured in stunning photos shared by observers worldwide.

summary: A total solar eclipse on Aug. 12, 2026, stunned skywatchers with a dramatic photo capturing the moment just before totality. The event was highlighted as Space.com's photo of the day for Aug. 13, 2026.

summary: The WorldView-3 Earth-observing satellite was launched into orbit on August 13, 2014. It marked a significant advancement in commercial Earth observation capabilities.

summary: The latest episode of 'Strange New Worlds' features a doppelganger story, continuing a tradition of 'Star Trek' narratives involving lookalikes. The episode explores themes of identity and duality within the sci-fi universe.

summary: A Chinese launch failure on August 10 preceded a busy week of international launches across three countries. The incident highlighted the challenges in spaceflight amid a packed launch schedule.

summary: Blue Origin is nearing the resolution of its investigation into a catastrophic engine explosion. The company is also planning for a dual launch pad future.

summary: Relativity Space achieved a key milestone in integrating engines for the first stage of its reusable Terran-R rocket. This development advances the company's progress toward the rocket's maiden launch.

summary: NASA has moved up the launch date for the Crew-13 mission to the ISS. The Crew-13 pilot shared insights on their career, training, and upcoming scientific objectives.

summary: SpaceX is recovering Ship 40 after its soft landing in the Indian Ocean, while Ship 41 prepares for testing ahead of Flight 14.

summary: The first full week of August is expected to be busy with multiple launches, including Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions. The manifest highlights a significant activity in the space industry.

summary: Boeing's CST-100 Starliner spacecraft is undergoing redesign work for a potential cargo mission to the International Space Station (ISS) by 2026. Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg highlighted the ongoing efforts to address previous issues with the spacecraft.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona. This approach allows scientists to gather more data than a natural eclipse would permit.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This presents a unique opportunity for testing innovative software in a real deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency's technical center in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to block the Sun's light, creating an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona. This involves two satellites playing a 'hide and seek' game to achieve precise alignment.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on 16-17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands will bring together startup companies and Europe's space industry to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaboration opportunities.

summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technology for next-generation antennas. It highlights how these innovations are driving improvements in antenna performance and efficiency.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: The European Space Agency's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber at ESTEC, confirming its electronics are fit for space. The mission is scheduled to launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted a successful test firing, marking a significant advancement in eco-friendly space propulsion technology. This development highlights the industry's shift toward sustainable chemical propulsion systems.

summary: A Space Force official shared insights on what startups should highlight or avoid when pitching for award opportunities. The discussion focused on identifying green and red flags in applications.

summary: Astranis developed Perceptor, a Space Domain Awareness (SDA) product for GEO, to address issues with existing SDA technology. This innovation aims to enhance monitoring and management in geostationary orbit.

title: Firefly Announces Record Q2 Results
summary: Firefly Aerospace reported its first-ever quarterly revenue exceeding $100 million, driven by new launch and defense contracts. The company announced multiple agreements to bolster its financial performance.

title: Guetlein: CR Could Mean ‘No Golden Dome…No Funding’
summary: A senior official warned that without a budget agreement, critical space programs like the 'Golden Dome' may face funding shortages. Failure to resolve budget issues could lead to significant financial shortfalls for space initiatives.

summary: A bipartisan group of senators introduced the Space Superiority Readiness Act to prepare the US military for potential conflicts in space involving China. The bill aims to enhance the country's readiness in orbital warfare.

summary: Rocket Lab introduced GHOST, a deployable launch system for responsive global launches. The announcement coincided with the company's record quarter.

summary: Astrolight and ATMOS have partnered to conduct a laser communications demonstration onboard ATMOS' PHOENIX 2 reentry vehicle in 2027. This collaboration aims to advance communication technologies for reentry missions.

summary: MDA Space plans to adapt its Canadarm3 robotic arm technology for lunar surface operations following NASA's pause on the Gateway program. The company aims to leverage its existing microgravity robotics expertise for new lunar missions.

summary: Europe's IRIS2 constellation has entered the build phase after seven months of negotiations between the European Commission, ESA, EUSPA, and SpaceRISE. This marks a significant step toward implementation.

summary: The Rwanda Government is partnering with Planet Labs to launch a new national program leveraging satellite technology for government and public services. Planet Labs will provide support to enhance these initiatives.

summary: Mantis Space has appointed Dale Parkes, a former Boeing executive, as its new Chief Technology Officer. The appointment coincides with the company's development of a spacecraft constellation designed for near-continuous Earth orbit operations.

title: Telesat Remains Optimistic About Lightspeed Despite Shaky 1H26 Financial Results, Looming Debt
summary: Telesat remains optimistic about its Lightspeed satellite constellation despite reporting weak financial results for the first half of 2026 and facing concerns over upcoming debt obligations.

title: Optus Completes First Part of Project Aurora
summary: Optus, an Australian telecommunications and satellite company, has completed the first phase of Project Aurora, a satellite life extension initiative.

title: Marlink to Acquire U.K. Defense Comms Specialist GRC
summary: Marlink is acquiring the U.K.-based defense communications specialist GRC to strengthen its position in European government, defense, and critical infrastructure markets. The acquisition aims to enhance Marlink's capabilities in these sectors.

title: Space42 and Leonardo DRS to Boost UAE National Security
summary: Space42 and Leonardo DRS have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance national security capabilities in the UAE. The agreement involves Leonardo DRS contributing its expertise to support the initiative.

title: Rocket Lab Margins Under the Microscope Following 2Q Earnings
summary: Rocket Lab faced investor scrutiny after releasing its second-quarter earnings, with a focus on its financial margins. The company's earnings report drew attention from the space industry and financial analysts.

title: DamoTech Joins Space ISAC
summary: DamoTech has joined the Space Information Sharing and Analysis Center (Space ISAC) to enhance cybersecurity collaboration in the space sector. The company specializes in advanced cybersecurity solutions for space applications.

title: U.S. Space Force Selects Voyager Technologies for Space-to-Space Communications Development Award
summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded Voyager Technologies a contract to develop space-to-space communication capabilities for Space Systems Command. This marks a significant advancement in military space communications.
